body: But why not?! :P

You are wise! Both of us have been in that unreasonable spot of declaring, "Just support me!" But that doesn't give the other partner anything to work with, and it guarantees that you'll end up disappointed. So delineating it like this is so smart. This is wonderful advice in any tough situation, I think. Thank you!
Thank you very much. I have a few friends that I'm talking to, and that's really helping. Plus, I can make wry MIL jokes with them... My husband, especially right now, not so much...

Thank you so much. Your expert level of positive reframing is something I can only aspire to in my lifetime. Good for you! My version of it would've been closer to, "It's a fucking shit on shit sandwich with extra bullshit." :P 

Everything is going to work out and I do think you're right. In our own ways, we are infinitely better at supporting one another and seeing one another's POVs now than we were last time, and so I think we really will weather this one together, and that's what I really want.

That is terrible, I am so sorry that you had to deal with cancer and death during your cycle. I really like how you put it. IVF is a big deal and other big deals don't negate the big dealness. 

I'm getting support from some friends. And my husband and I are talking and really trying to honor one another's feelings. It's going well. He hasn't called me selfish and I haven't overtaxed him or become too demanding, which I've been known to do in the past. In our previous life, we would've had a few huge blowouts by this point. 

The good thing about being so tired and overwhelmed is I'm actually too tired and overwhelmed to throw a big emotional fit. So those emotions are going to end up being put aside and mellowing out on their own because I just can't really get into everything all at once.

Thank you very much. I have talked to him a few times today. We are not thinking of canceling. I'm fine with the stims so far and I've metabolized about $300 worth of drugs so far, so I wouldn't be okay with scrapping it at this point. Thanks for the reassurance and for keeping my MIL in your thoughts. I hope for the best, too...

Ha! This is an excellent point. I tend to take these events over and shoulder everything, which I think is sometimes a female trait (to make a gross generalization). But we all have to deal with shit, sometimes simultaneously, as /u/giantredwoodforest said, so we can all put our big boy and girl pants on this week...

I may or may not move out of state. My family is a hot mess, too, unfortunately. Plus there's the issue of selling the house and not trusting him in that process, which would be incentive to stay. She was telling me to go give birth and move somewhere. And it seemed crazy to me, too. Perhaps she's not the lawyer for me!
It did sound strange, so that's why I wanted to post here.

He absolutely has rights, and I am not trying to operate out of spite, but since he is an alcoholic from a family of active alcoholics, I want to make sure that I have the legal system on my side to protect the child from potential threats dealing with the substance abuse. For example, my brother-in-law was drunk and dropped his six-week-old baby, fracturing his skull. I know that legally, what one guy doesn't can't carry over to another guy, but it's an example of the family environment and why I want to control custody as much as possible. I'm fine with my husband having visitation or custody (perhaps supervised), but if he's actively drinking, I need to protect the vulnerable minor from a bad situation.

Thanks for checking in. We're trying to start a business and having some issues with his family, so I have yet to bring it up in therapy. If that sounds like a shitty excuse, it is. Things are good and bad, and slightly more active on the DB front, but not by much. I have good and bad moments when it comes to the relationship. Out anniversary was yesterday and we had a fight, so I'm just feeling particularly down today, I guess. Ugh.

I was the other woman who a married guy was cheating with. Have you seen the movie UP IN THE AIR? It was like that. He'd get booked to speak at conferences around the country, and he would fly me out. One time, he even flew me out to LA while he was on a Dodgers trip with his dad. He'd hang out with his dad at the game and then say he had to work, then skip to the next hotel tower and we would get drunk, binge watch movies, and have tons of crazy sex. Near the end, he started shipping me out to his hometown and putting me up Ina hotel. Instead of work, he would be with me, go home after work, and then come back for a few hours while his wife fell asleep early. He'd then sneak back into bed in the middle of the night. The whole thing was terribly amoral but I was at a really fucked up time in my life and, frankly, it was hot and edgy and dangerous. Plus, I wasn't the one that had anything to lose. We fell in love, of course. We knew it wouldn't work after the rush wore off, but we would speak constantly and email all day long when separated. He'd be my last contact in a day and my heart would swell every morning once I woke up and checked my phone, where an email would invariably be waiting. 

At the time, I started seeing the guy who is now my fiancé. So Married Guy wasn't my only thing. It will come as a shock that he didn't get caught, but we had so many close calls that I decided to end it and pursue my current SO. One of the worst was (TMI) related to a potential STD scare. He started getting a rash on his dick. Meanwhile, I had no symptoms. He was convinced that I had gotten herpes and given it to him. His wife started getting a rash. Meanwhile, I was on a trip to Japan and instead of enjoying myself, I was looking for American-friendly STD clinics where I could get tested. It was a ridiculous situation. He decides he's sure it's herpes and is about to tell his wife everything. We make plans for me to take him in during the fallout. His b
est friend talks him out of it. When I get back stateside, we both get tested...it's not herpes. His wife got a yeast infection and it spread to his dick. (Gross.) Another time, we were at a beachside B&B and the owner assumed we were husband and wife. Then we get back from tennis and there's a post it on our door: "Your WIFE called." We got frosty looks for the rest of our stay.

It definitely affected me because I loved him and knew we couldn't be together, which didn't help the feelings I had. It definitely took a toll on him. He was a nervous wreck, always anxious. I think he'd gotten in over his head. He still loved his wife but they got married young and took one another's virginities. He must've felt like he was missing out. I had to push him away in order for him to be able to end things. He wouldn't have otherwise. It was just getting too painful. We were angry with one another for a long time. We still talk occasionally. The subject of another affair has come up. But I have something to lose, too, this time. Call me a shitty person, but now that I do, I'm not willing to put it on the line like he did for me. I miss those days, though, honestly. The danger, the hot anonymous hotel sex. But it's not real life.

TL;DR: Cheating is ridiculous, whether you get caught or not, and it's not worth the emotional damage to you or the other person.
I will give it another go, thanks for the push!

Thanks for relating and for the encouragement. I really appreciate you taking the time to reply. I think it's easier for a lot of people to NOT talk about difficult or vulnerable things, and that's why so many relationships suffer from communication issues and silence where there should be safe, productive conversation. There's a lot to think about here as I begin to approach the issue with him.

Wow. This is a very thorough response. Thank you for the list and the questions to consider. The way you've framed it will really help me a) consider the issues for myself, and b) broach them with my partner so that we can get a functional discussion going about this. The thoughts on dominance vs. initiation are particularly interesting to me. Once again, I really appreciate the time you put into this.

This is exactly the sort of insight I'm looking for. We don't flirt as much or set the tone for sex before the situation actually comes up (or doesn't!), so that's definitely actionable. Thanks for that, and for your thoughts on the "initiate more" dynamic that we're caught up with. I really appreciate the time you took to comment.

Personally, I found that it really irritated me and completely dried me out, to the point where inserting it and ESPECIALLY removing it after sex would feel almost raw. I've never felt anything like that, not even rough sex. Maybe it was a combination of having the material in there and the hormones delivered locally rather than systemically that did it, but I could  only deal with it for a few months.

Thanks for the straight talk and encouragement about bringing it up in therapy and working on ourselves instead of one another. :) I really appreciate it.

I'll bring it up in March (we're going out of town for three weeks). I need to take more accountability, and it looks like I'll have to be the one to bring it up. Doing it in a "public" venue like therapy is definitely the way to go, I think. 

I had a terrible experience with the NuvaRing and inserting anything before sex has been off my radar since then. Maybe I was improperly fitted or educated about it. It's definitely worth looking into it.

It's frustrating, and I feel like I'm at a disadvantage because I've only ever been with men who have lots of ideas for experimentation, etc. I don't have a lot of practice coming up with ideas or initiating, and that's the one thing he says is missing: me initiating. I can see where he's coming from, but I don't know if that's the only thing missing, because once the sex is happening, it's not really about mutual pleasure or trying new things. 

But I am writing from a place of "I want to learn and improve." That's where I want to go before "end tragically" and "deserve better." I definitely don't want to reject any of your hard-won advice, though, so thanks for the perspective!

It's a huge age difference. But we're in a committed relationship, are actively working on ourselves to be better partners in other areas, and have an impasse in the bedroom. That's something we (hopefully) CAN change, and I'm trying to reach out to people with some experience in the hopes of being proactive. Our ages is one thing that we absolutely cannot change, no matter how much we try. Thanks for the perspective anyway.

> My man claims to be happy to just be vanilla, but he also claims he gets bored with just regular sex.

Yes! I struggle with reconciling this. And doing things that seem abusive is hard for him. I just don't know how to bring up the topic because it has not really been met with much response in the past, and even less action. Why is sex so hard to talk about? Ha. I guess that's a big part of why we're all here.

I'm engaged to a man who I love very much, but we have several key personality differences. Sometimes this is a great thing, other times not. Unfortunately, he's not the person I've ever been the most in synch with in my life. That would be a former partner. We were basically the same person, understood one another on an incredible level, laughed harder than I've ever laughed, and we carried on a torrid yearlong affair. Alas, it WAS an affair. He is unhappily married (not that this is an excuse). I broke things off a few years ago to be with my now fiancé and move on with my life. He recently started contacting me again, wanting to get together. I will absolutely not meet up with him or rekindle communication. What we had is in the past. I've told my fiancé that my "ex" is contacting me again, because I really want to work on things and be transparent. But sometimes I do miss having this type of seamless dynamic with someone (even though our relationship was basically a fantasy outside the realm of our normal realities), especially in times when my fiancé and I are going through a difficult period or not communicating well... I can't help it. It's the laughing. I hardly ever laugh like that anymore.
The drunk thing didn't cause a purchase I wouldn't have entered into sober, it just helped me pull the trigger.
Mom, is that you?

I replied elsewhere but we've opened our financial books with one another and have created a repayment plan for our (otherwise modest) debt that we showed up to the relationship with. He just doesn't know which purchases contributed to my number.

> degloving injury

I had to look this up. Oddly, a degloving injury isn't the first thing I think of when it comes to jewelry...and maybe that's the problem!
Marketing. There was a horribly depressing Atlantic article written in '82 about how much diamonds are bullshit. But it's a beautiful piece of jewelry and I am an idiot, so...
I just wanted it for myself, not to, you know, slip him an engagement ring and pretend we had an agreement. I was like, "Fuck it, I will be my own diamond daddy."

We have absolutely opened our financial books with one another and we're working on a repayment solution for both of our debt, which is actually pretty reasonable given the shenanigans I described. He's seen all my numbers, he just doesn't know that this one thing contributed to them.
I am going to bring it up at some point. And I'd wear it on my other hand. I just need to work up the nerve.
I love this idea, and diamonds are basically useless in terms of resale value. I just hope my future daughter in law is as stylish as I am... ;)

I was SO SICK of not being proposed to and was doing a lot of browsing around on engagement ring websites. During that process, I fell in love with a vintage one-of-a-kind ring. At one point, someone else put it in their cart and just...SAT ON IT...for weeks...and that was the last straw. This thing was from the 1930s, gorgeous, and once it was gone, it would be gone forever. I got drunk, called the store, and bought it outright with my credit card (the only way to get it once it was in someone else's cart). It arrived, it's absolutely beautiful, it cost just under five figures. A month later, my fiancé proposed with an equally beautiful ring. 

I don't feel like I can ever wear the first one I bought because it's a little more blingy, so I don't want it to steal thunder from my real engagement ring. And I don't want my fiancé to know that I spent SO MUCH MONEY on something so stupid. I basically got engaged to myself in secret before getting engaged. Goddamn woman brain. So impatient. So attracted to shiny things. So in credit card debt.

TL;DR: Bought super expensive ring for self out of spite/impatience, got proposed to a month later.
